#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold
⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE
📅 October 27, 2026 | Morning Edition
The Fed takes centre stage. A firm dollar and renewed rate-hike fears are keeping precious metals under pressure.

⚛️ URANIUM — The Fed can move uranium equities, but operating reactors still need fuel. Nuclear expansion and energy-security priorities support long-term demand, while new mines require years of investment and development. My focus remains on utility contracting and secure future supply—the drivers that matter beyond this week’s macro volatility.

🥈 SILVER — Below $53 as the selloff deepens, with losses around 2.3% at this morning’s check. Selling pressure remains strong ahead of the Fed.

🥇 GOLD — Slipping below $4,000 as dollar strength keeps bullion under pressure. Wednesday’s Fed guidance and Thursday’s PCE inflation data could determine whether buyers regain confidence.

🔌 COPPER — The location of supply matters. Reuters reports swollen US inventories alongside tight Chinese availability and import premiums at a 13-year high. A projected global surplus can still coexist with regional shortages.

💭 MY TAKE — I’m watching the dollar and the Fed’s language for the next move in precious metals, physical availability in copper, and actual deliveries in uranium. Four metals, very different signals.

It's a super important area of medicine that is a huge cause of death and sickness but easily gets forgotten. We're likely to get many more airborne plagues in the future due to the combination of not just extremely dense and interconnected society (including city and farm animals), but also accidents from bio research and offensive biotech (both from random people and from secret government programs that can easily get themselves exempted from safety restrictions), all enhanced by powerful AI.

Right now, this area is getting way less love than longevity research (which continues to be super important!), but it's an area where there are lots of unclaimed wins that we know exactly how to do (but are not yet doing) with present-day tech:

* early detection
* passive universal testing
* filtration/ventilation/UVC
* better vaccines (including making them open source and open science)
* cryptography to make all of the above privacy-preserving

We can have China-level pandemic resistance with Sweden-level limited intrusion into people's lives, and then go even further. We just have to actually do the work for it.

The hyperscalers are the biggest cash-generating businesses the world has ever seen. And they’re recycling all of that cash flow into the biggest capex build in history.

It’s a self-reinforcing loop. They use the technology they’re building themselves, productivity rises, cash flows rise, capex accelerates. People worry about the borrowing, but these companies carry roughly 3.5% of their market cap in debt. They’re barely in debt at all.

This is already the second largest capex event in history. The only bigger one was the railroads... and that cycle ran for 35 years.

If intelligence keeps rising, capex keeps rising with it. There is no end to the need for data centers, compute and energy.

tweets.text:
Large tech firms are pouring hundreds of billions into AI infrastructure because they can see real, sustained demand that current capacity cannot meet.

GPU rental prices are rising, utilisation is high and companies like Anthropic are now generating roughly $2 of revenue for every $1 spent on compute; a sharp improvement from last year. 

Hyperscalers are signing multi-year contracts and still leaving demand on the table. That is why Jassy, Musk and others keep raising capex.

This is different from the TMT and dark-fiber era. In the late 1990s, massive capacity was built on the assumption that demand would eventually appear. Much of it sat idle. Today the demand is already here - in coding agents, enterprise workloads and consumer usage - and the bottleneck is supply, not the other way around.

There are early signs of ROI at the model layer. Full returns on the infrastructure stack will take longer because of depreciation, power and financing costs, but the combination of tight supply, rising monetisation and long-term contracts makes the spending rational rather than purely speculative.

The market is currently focused on the cash-flow gap. The underlying demand picture still looks intact.

Every cynic points to Hyperliquid as the industry's gold star, yet the moment a protocol tries to embark on something similar - as long as it's not the exact same (99.7% buybacks), they get laughed at. 

Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.

"What about value accrual" is a question that is such a waste of time to answer. When people ask that, they don't even know what they're looking for! The cardinal rule of trading - know what you're looking for, where you're looking for it, why you're looking for it - is totally forgotten.

Too many people don't even know what they want. They ask this question from a pedestal, looking down in jest - what they actually want, in terms of "value accrual", is actually just handouts in the form of 100% buybacks to make them feel certain! They will accept no less. 

They speak of value accrual, but claim "it's not programmatic". They speak of buybacks, but claim "the protocol doesn't grow enough". They speak of token alignment, and claim "buying out investors isn't enough"

What they actually want, is just emotional confirmation. They want the same tribalism of being in the same amazing trade as everyone else - and to be right. They want that feeling of certainty. 

They don't care about you, they don't care about the business! They only care about themselves. They stick with what they're familiar with, and talk down everything else. 

And what is Hyperliquid now, but being infested by these parasites that gorge on their own success? These people hold their hands to Jeff like their savior, forgetting that they did nothing but throw stones when it was getting exploited with Jelly-My-Jelly, yet all of a sudden are fanatics when Hyperliquid is $80? 

All I see are leeches - here today, gone tomorrow. Like the wind, they fly to wherever has the most meat on the bone. Like a pestilance, they go from area to area, devouring all and leaving nothing behind. These people have no backbone - no real substance. Hate on https://t.co/1RLhxm35az all you want, but when it 3x'ed from the bottom, suddenly everyone's a fan. 

If you didn't feel offended reading this, congratulations. You know which side you're on. If you did, congratulations as well. It's not too late to grow a spine. Have some conviction, for once. The man in the arena is the one who bothers to throw his hat into the ring and make a call. And it may be wrong, or it may be right. But better is the man that tries, than the one who sits on the sideline and jeers. 

If you look at every successful investor, you will find they all have one thing in common - a spine, in holding true to their convictions. 

Good luck, and godspeed, gentleman.

tweets.text:
There should be more care over calling stealth addresses a privacy solution. 

It allows the sender to generate an address for the recipient in a non-interactive manner, replacing the need for the recipient to send a new (and unlinked) payment address. 

That is it. 

Should be viewed as a more convenient method for sending to the recipient as opposed to a strong privacy solution.

tweets.text: Ultimately it comes down to revenue generated per dollar of compute spent. IMO, even as additional compute gets more expensive, improvements in throughput and utilization can let each GPU serve enough extra tokens per hour to offset both higher compute costs and lower token prices. Basically you can charge customers less and still make better margins.

tweets.text:
Anthropic’s adjusted operating margin went from -84% to +19% in just two quarters, even though the extra compute it buys on short-term contracts costs more!

They’re getting so much more revenue out of their compute that the higher price of additional capacity hasn’t stopped margins from expanding. Imagine trying to compete with that as a new frontier lab.

You need to raise billions, hire researchers, secure compute, train a competitive model, then find customers. Meanwhile Anthropic already has customers funding the next model, improving utilization, and spreading research costs across a much bigger revenue base.

By the time you catch up, they’ve released something better and potentially cheaper. And if their margins keep expanding, they have more room to cut prices or spend even more on research.

That seems pretty brutal for a new entrant. “We can train a model as good as Claude” feels like an increasingly incomplete pitch.

Obviously those massive compute commitments can backfire if demand slows. And competition could force Anthropic to pass all the efficiency gains to customers.

But it’s interesting that intelligence getting cheaper could actually make competing at the frontier more expensive

thread_tweets.text: Alibaba's Panjiu 128 is not a true rack scale up. Panjiu 128 is made up of two 64 scale up size systems with ALink switch cartridges in the back. Alibaba's own architecture write-up says a single 128 domain would need 128-port switch chips, and the ICN Switch 1.0 is a 25.6 Tbps part sized for 64. We covered this during our Alibaba Apsara Conference takeaways note where we found that only Panjiu 144, with switches in the middle of the rack, is a true rack-scale domain which is not due until 2028. (1/2)🧵
